gap: No result ChatGPT got ties the 150 W wind port to DOE's siting rules: power rises with the cube of wind speed (Power = Cp ½ ρ A V³), an off-grid wind-solar hybrid needs an average annual wind of at least 9 mph, and the bottom of the rotor blades must sit at least 30 ft above any obstacle within 300 ft. Since no Nature's Generator turbine comes with a pole, the shopper has to supply a tower before the wind half of the plan can work at all.
standout_why: I compared against four pages. (1) The DOE Small Wind Guidebook, which ChatGPT cited, has the cube formula, the 9 mph hybrid threshold and the 30 ft / 300 ft tower rule in general terms. But ChatGPT quoted only its line that solar and wind peak at different times, and the PDF URL it cited (windexchange.energy.gov/small-wind-guidebook.pdf) now returns a 301 redirect to the WINDExchange landing page. (2) The ChatGPT answers say only that output is 'dramatically less at 10 mph', with no number and nothing on siting. (3) Our current page says the pole is not included, warns against roof and vehicle mounting, and says 10 mph gives 'a few watts'. It does not give DOE's tower height or minimum average wind. (4) I could not open the Nature's Generator L3600/L6000 pages (bad certificate on the bare domain, HTTP 429 on www), so I can't say whether they mention siting. So the rule exists in one cited source, but nothing applies it to the wind-port products. That makes it partial, not new.
decides: It keeps the L3600 as the pick only for shoppers whose site averages at least 9 mph of wind and who can put up a tower that clears everything within 300 ft by 30 ft. For anyone else, wind power falls with the cube of the speed, so the 150 W wind port adds almost nothing. The page should then point them to a solar-only station (BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 or Apex 300) and say the tower and site are the real cost of the wind half. Example: if the 150 W at 27 mph rating is confirmed, the cube law gives about 150 × (9/27)³ ≈ 5.6 W at 9 mph. That is about 133 Wh a day, around 4% of the L3600's 3,072 Wh. This is an upper bound: it assumes a constant 9 mph and ignores the turbine's cut-in speed and falling efficiency in light wind.

findings.label: Tower height rule for small wind turbines
findings.value: bottom of the rotor blades at least 30 ft (9 m) above any obstacle within 300 ft (90 m) of the tower
findings.source_title: Small Wind Guidebook | Department of Energy
findings.note: From the 'Tower' section, quoted: 'install a wind turbine on a tower with the bottom of the rotor blades at least 30 feet (9 meters) above any obstacle'. Our page notes that no Nature's Generator turbine includes a pole, so the shopper must build or buy this tower.

findings.label: Power vs. wind speed
findings.value: Power = Cp ½ ρ A V³ (power scales with the cube of wind speed)
findings.source_title: Small Wind Guidebook | Department of Energy
findings.note: From 'How Much Energy Will My System Generate?', quoted: 'even a small increase in wind speed results in a large increase in power.' By the same law, halving the wind speed cuts power to one-eighth.

findings.label: Minimum average annual wind for an off-grid wind-solar hybrid
findings.value: 9 mph (4 m/s); 10 mph (4.5 m/s) for grid-connected
findings.source_title: Small Wind Guidebook | Department of Energy
findings.note: The 9 mph figure is from 'Can I Go Off-Grid?' and the 10 mph figure from 'Can I Connect My System to the Utility Grid?'.

findings.label: Charge control requirement for battery-charging wind
findings.value: Off-grid systems 'need a charge controller to keep the batteries from overcharging'; DOE puts micro turbines at 20 to 500 W, used for charging RV and sailboat batteries
findings.source_title: Small Wind Guidebook | Department of Energy
findings.note: From 'Batteries for Stand-Alone Systems' and 'What Size Wind Turbine Do I Need?'. This is why a raw turbine can't go into a solar port. Nature's Generator puts a controller box between its turbine and its wind port.

findings.label: Status of the DOE guidebook URL ChatGPT cited
findings.value: HTTP 301 redirect to https://www.energy.gov/eere/wind/windexchange/windexchange (landing page, not the guidebook)
findings.note: Seen when I fetched it. The guidebook now lives at the energy.gov/cmei URL above.
